A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoSA framework, CoSAlign method, and benchmarks. All 32 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model experiments, CoSApien human evaluation, general capability and safety results, and supplementary analyses in Tables 1–7 and Figures 3 and 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds results for two CoSAlign filtering variants in Table 3.

M1.justification: Table 3 adds evaluated CoSAlign inference variants using Cascade and Cascade-Oracle safety filtering after generation. These are limited compositions with an existing filtering procedure; the underlying taxonomy construction, preference-data synthesis, error scoring, and SFT/DPO training remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training retains BeaverTails and non-adversarial WildguardTrain prompts. Evaluation retains CoSAlign-Test, the same five CoSApien scenarios, and the same general capability and safety benchmarks. The filtering variants introduce no new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 expands its comparison set with L3.1-8B-INST+CoSAlign+Cascade and L3.1-8B-INST+CoSAlign+Cascade-Oracle. All previously evaluated ICA, Cascade, safety-removed, and CoSAlign variants are retained.

E3.justification: The evaluation protocol retains the same seen/unseen configurations, 3,200 CoSAlign-Test prompts, 200 CoSApien prompts, metrics, and judging procedures. The added filtering variants use this existing protocol; no revision to splits, training settings, or evaluation budgets is reported.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a comparison of unfiltered CoSAlign with ordinary and oracle filtering, testing filtering's effect on helpfulness and safety. Existing shot-count, SFT/DPO, LoRA, and disallowed-content analyses remain unchanged, including Appendix Table 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the model results. Human annotation and agreement-reporting procedures are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged. Table 3 adds seen/unseen CoSA-Scores of 0.368/0.274 for CoSAlign+Cascade and 0.454/0.364 for CoSAlign+Cascade-Oracle, alongside retained unfiltered scores of 0.408/0.293. Corresponding helpful+safe and helpful+unsafe rates are added. These are new variant results, not improvements from rerunning an unchanged model.

T1.justification: The safety-config definitions, CoSA-Score formula, risk-set relationships, and error-scoring mathematics are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is relocated without mathematical revision; neither version adds theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same contributions and claims about inference-time safety adaptation, CoSAlign's controllability and generalization, CoSA-Score, and CoSApien. The added filtering results do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning DPO, generalization, rare risks, partial requests, and LoRA remain substantively unchanged. The existing ethics and limitations discussions move to Appendices A.1–A.2. No substantive interpretation of the new filtering rows is added.

D1.justification: v1's Section 7 promises future release of code, datasets, and checkpoints; v2 removes that paragraph and adds a project-page link on page 1. Hardware, hyperparameters, and implementation instructions remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish artifact availability at the link.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Huang et al. on in-context alignment, Guo et al. on controllable preference optimization, Yang et al. on Rewards-in-Context, and Yin et al. on SafeWorld. These modestly extend related-work coverage while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording edits, merges the ICA setup paragraph, and moves ethics and limitations into the appendix with updated cross-references. It also adds conference identification and an equal-advising note. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains two rows and changes numerical emphasis. Algorithm 1 moves from the main text to Appendix A.5, and existing figures and tables shift position. Conference headers and local reflow alter presentation, while the figures themselves retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new Table 3 comparisons address whether safety filtering complements CoSAlign, a combination untested in v1. They reveal that ordinary filtering reduces helpful+unsafe responses while sacrificing helpfulness and CoSA-Score, whereas oracle filtering improves the measured tradeoff. This modestly strengthens the empirical analysis, although the new results receive little discussion and the main reporting limitations remain unchanged.
